circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island designed by Hermann Tilke, has served as the venue for the final round of the Formula One World Championship since 2009. It became the second Middle Eastern Formula One facility, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne that hosts the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various supporting racing categories. Holding an FIA Grade 1 classification, the venue serves as a premier motorsport destination in the city.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit has hosted the Austrian Grand Prix across two distinct periods: first as the Österreichring from 1970 to 1987, then following significant modifications and a renaming as the A1-Ring from 1997 to 2003. The track underwent substantial changes between these two eras, including a reduction in length and complete reconstruction.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street venue in Azerbaijan's capital that spans 6. 003 kilometers, ranking among the longest tracks in Formula One racing. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming a permanent fixture on the calendar with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix ever held in the Middle East that same year. The FIA Grade 1 facility accommodates various motorsport series including GP2 and drag racing, with multiple track configurations available for different events and categories of competition.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers through Montmeló near Barcelona and features a balanced mix of straightaways and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for racing machinery. The facility holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Situated near Spa in the Wallonia region of Belgium, this 7. 004 km circuit is one of Formula One's most historic venues, having first hosted a Grand Prix in 1925 and featured prominently in the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The track has maintained an unbroken presence on the F1 calendar since 1985, except for absences in 2003 and 2006, and currently serves as the home of the Belgian Grand Prix.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that serves as the home of the Canadian Grand Prix in Formula One. Beyond its Formula One duties, the track has accommodated various other racing categories including international sportscar championships, open-wheel series, and North American stock car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility is primarily recognized as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before returning in 2024. The track has expanded its racing calendar to include an electric motorsport championship event starting in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, Silverstone has been England's premier racing venue since hosting the inaugural British Grand Prix in 1948. The circuit gained historical significance by staging the first-ever Formula One World Championship race in 1950, and after sharing the British Grand Prix with two other tracks for three decades, it became the permanent home of the event from 1987 onwards. Beyond Formula One, the track also serves as host to international motorcycle racing competitions.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest hosted Formula One's first Grand Prix behind the Iron Curtain in 1986, constructed in just eight months, a record for circuit-building speed at the time. Built outside the city rather than as a planned street circuit in a Budapest park, the 4. 381 km track held its inaugural race in tribute to János Drapál, a pioneering Hungarian motorcycle racing champion.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian racing circuit constructed in 1922 near Milan, earning the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its lengthy straights and fast-flowing layout. Home to the Italian Grand Prix since 1949 (with only a 1980 interruption for renovation), the track stands among the oldest continuously used Formula One venues, having hosted the championship through nearly every season of its existence.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Located in Mie Prefecture, Japan, the Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km track operated by Honda Mobilityland that hosts major international motorsport competitions. The facility, which accommodates 155,000 spectators, has become particularly renowned as a cornerstone venue for the Formula One World Championship and Japanese Super Formula racing series.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, utilizing roads adjacent to the famous Las Vegas Strip along Las Vegas Boulevard. The layout passes by iconic venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, weaving through the heart of the city's hotel and casino district.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Situated in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is named after two fatal racing drivers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue returned to hosting the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix from 2015 onwards after a 23-year absence, now competing under the Mexico City Grand Prix title since 2021, on a revised circuit configuration from its earlier hosting periods that ended in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and average qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by specialist circuit engineers, it was purpose-built to host the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022, and has since accommodated other motorsport series on adapted configurations.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, encircling Monaco's harbour. Despite its official name, the circuit is widely known as Monte Carlo since most of its layout occupies that particular neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the coastal dunes near Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km Dutch racing circuit hosted the Dutch Grand Prix following its Formula One return in 2021, though this arrangement concluded in 2026. The track, situated just north of Zandvoort and within sight of the North Sea, has operated under its current sponsorship designation since mid-2025.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a motor racing facility situated north of Doha in Qatar, spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a prominent 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features an associated kart facility dedicated to fellow racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: Situated along Jeddah's waterfront promenade beside the Red Sea, this street circuit has served as the venue for the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since 2021 and has recently begun hosting international electric racing events. The track's seaside location on the Corniche provides a distinctive setting for Formula One competition in the Middle East.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront district, incorporating the urban areas of both Downtown Core and Kallang in its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced mix of extended straights and varied corner configurations that test multiple driving skills. The venue, holding FIA Grade 1 status, accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of Formula One's United States Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track hosts various international racing series including MotoGP and sports car championships, while previously accommodating numerous other motorsport categories ranging from IndyCar to rallycross competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British driver currently racing for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 along with 32 Grand Prix victories throughout his 23-season career. Beyond the sport's premier category, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including victories at Le Mans, the 24 Hours of Daytona, and the World Endurance Championship, making him uniquely the only driver to win both a Formula One drivers' title and a World Endurance Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli, an Italian driver, made his Formula One debut in 2025 with Mercedes, where he currently competes. He has secured eight Grand Prix victories since entering the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabriel "Gabi" Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One for Audi, bringing his racing expertise to the German manufacturer's grid effort.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing over a decade of experience to the sport. He previously achieved two runner-up championship finishes during his time with Mercedes and has secured 10 race victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One for Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan races in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category with Nielsen Racing while holding a reserve role at Haas in Formula One, having made seven Grand Prix appearances during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved his sole grand prix victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while previously competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver competing for Red Bull Racing in Formula One, racing under the French flag.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: A British driver competing for Ferrari, Hamilton has secured seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record tally. He holds numerous racing records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg, a German driver competing for Audi in Formula One, has demonstrated his versatility across motorsport disciplines. Beyond his current F1 commitments, he achieved a major endurance racing milestone by winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: New Zealand driver Liam Lawson currently races in Formula One as part of the Racing Bulls lineup.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured second place in the 2022 championship standings. Across his nine seasons in the sport, Leclerc has claimed nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen, known as K-Mag, raced in Formula One across two separate stints between 2014 and 2024. He has since transitioned to sports car racing with BMW in the FIA World Endurance Championship while also competing part-time in NASCAR's Cup Series for Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British racing driver, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while competing for McLaren. Throughout his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The driver previously achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio "Checo" Pérez is a Mexican driver currently racing for Cadillac in Formula One. The experienced competitor finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull and has secured six race victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian Formula One driver currently racing for McLaren who has claimed nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his 14-year career in the sport. Known by his nickname "the Honey Badger," he established himself as a consistent competitor across multiple seasons before retiring from the championship.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz has competed in Formula One for over a decade, securing four race victories during his career. He currently races for Williams in the championship.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition. The former Formula One competitor, who drove in the series during 2023 and 2024, has since transitioned to sports car racing.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently competing in Formula One for Aston Martin, bringing his racing expertise to the team's competitive efforts on the grid.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently holding a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls. He competed as a full-time Formula One competitor from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve position in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has claimed four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12-season career, Verstappen has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently functioning as a reserve competitor for Cadillac in Formula One. He previously raced in the series from 2022 through 2024 and holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have participated in the championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team operated as Renault's factory entry in Formula One before rebranding to Alpine Racing Limited in 2021 to showcase the luxury sports car marque. The squad continued representing Renault until the manufacturer's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of the 2025 season.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin is a British manufacturer that has competed in Formula One through different organizational structures, with its current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, stands as Formula One's oldest continuously competing team and its most accomplished, having entered every World Championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. The squad, colloquially called "the Prancing Horse" for its iconic emblem, remains a cornerstone institution in motorsport history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with the squad entering the sport for the 2016 season. Ayao Komatsu currently leads the team as principal, taking over from Guenther Steiner who held the position from the team's establishment through early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering firm founded in 1970, the Sauber team built sports cars and Formula One machinery as an independent constructor, highlighted by Le Mans success and two world championships in endurance racing. After competing in Formula One from 1993 onwards through various iterations, the squad departed the sport in 2025 as one of the championship's longest-serving constructors before being acquired by Audi to establish the foundation for its factory team.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One team headquartered in Woking that competes under the McLaren Mastercard F1 Team banner. As a subsidiary of the McLaren Group, the team is owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with its current team based in Brackley and operating under a German licence. The operation became a three-way partnership in 2022 involving Mercedes-Benz, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff as equal stakeholders. The marque is traditionally associated with the "Silver Arrows" nickname in racing.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team that began competing in 2024 as a second constructor under Red Bull's ownership. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates alongside Red Bull Racing as part of the automotive conglomerate's dual-team strategy in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in the 2024 season as part of Red Bull GmbH's dual-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team functions as Red Bull's second constructor in the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England but operating under an Austrian licence, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 and has become one of two racing operations within the Red Bull GmbH conglomerate. Under Christian Horner's leadership from its inception through 2024, the team established itself as a major force in the sport before Horner's departure led to Laurent Mekies assuming the management role. The squad operates alongside the Red Bull-owned Racing Bulls team within the broader corporate structure.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Atlassian Williams F1 Team is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's previous unsuccessful racing venture. Headquartered on a substantial facility in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team has established itself as a significant player in the sport's engineering and competitive landscape.
